Set up an editable Shiny demo for a cloud workspace

Source: R/cloud-demo.R
oauth_db_cloud_demo.Rd

A console guide helps you find your workspace and OAuth app settings, then runs a local Shiny app with your installed R packages. Visitors sign in through shinyOAuth and use their own cloud data permissions.

Usage

oauth_db_cloud_demo(
  platform = "databricks",
  host = NULL,
  client_id = NULL,
  client_type = NULL,
  warehouse_id = NULL,
  http_path = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  port = NULL,
  edition = NULL,
  action = c("start", "files"),
  prompt = interactive(),
  launch_browser = interactive(),
  ...
)

Arguments

platform

Cloud platform: "databricks", "fabric", "bigquery", "snowflake", "azure-sql", "azure-postgres", "redshift" or "clickhouse".

host

Databricks workspace hostname or browser URL. Paths, queries and fragments are removed. For other SQL demos, an alias for server.

client_id

Client ID from your custom OAuth app registration.

client_type

"public" for PKCE without a secret, or "confidential". The guide asks when needed; noninteractive calls default to "public" where supported. BigQuery and Snowflake demos use confidential registrations.

warehouse_id

Optional default Databricks SQL warehouse ID.

http_path

Optional Databricks warehouse HTTP path, instead of warehouse_id.

path

Empty or existing cloud-demo directory. The default is a platform-specific directory in R's user cache, so drafts survive restarting R. Existing settings and app edits are preserved. Use a new empty path for a separate setup or fresh templates.

port

Local Shiny port, default 8100 or the saved setting. Register http://localhost:<port> exactly as the OAuth callback.

edition

Databricks only: "workspace", "trial", "free", or "unknown". Free Edition lacks the account-level custom registration this example needs.

action

"start" guides setup and runs the app; "files" writes an editable draft without network calls or asking for a secret.

prompt

Ask interactively for missing settings. Use FALSE in scripts.

launch_browser

Open the local app in a regular browser.

...

Named platform settings. Fabric uses server, database, tenant_id and optionally driver. Missing required values are explained and requested interactively. BigQuery uses project and optionally location and maximum_bytes_billed. Snowflake uses server, role, warehouse and optionally database, schema, driver. Azure SQL uses server, database, tenant_id and optionally driver, database_port (the SQL port, distinct from the local Shiny port). Azure PostgreSQL uses server, database, user, sslrootcert, tenant_id and optionally database_port. Redshift uses identity_center_ready, server, database, tenant_id, resource, scope and optionally driver, database_port. ClickHouse uses jwt_ready, url, tenant_id, resource, scope and optionally database. The Redshift and ClickHouse examples use Entra and require an existing trusted-token integration. See the platform's source guide, linked from vignette("getting-started", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Value

Invisibly, the demo directory, including after pausing incomplete interactive setup. Noninteractive starts report missing settings as errors.

Details

All demos use local R, bslib and processx. Install askpass for masked input. BigQuery and ClickHouse use jsonlite without a native database driver. Snowflake, Azure SQL and Redshift use odbc and their native ODBC drivers; Azure PostgreSQL uses RPostgres and a trusted CA bundle. Each copied app waits for an explicit query-button click. Stopping the local process does not stop shared cloud compute or cancel submitted jobs.

Fabric asks for its SQL server/database and an Entra tenant and app registration. Install fabricQueryR, odbc and Microsoft ODBC Driver 18. Its confidential secret uses OAUTHDB_FABRIC_CLIENT_SECRET. The copied app.R contains the connection and query code; demo-ui.R contains the UI.

Databricks needs an account-level custom OAuth app registration with the exact callback and SQL access. Public PKCE registrations need no secret. For confidential apps, set OAUTHDB_DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET or use the masked prompt. Secrets and tokens are not written to the generated files or serialized R arguments. The app's child process receives the secret through its environment. Normal cloud TLS verification stays enabled.

Settings can also come from OAUTHDB_DATABRICKS_HOST and OAUTHDB_DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID. The guide can pause for registration and resume from path. The generated settings.dcf contains only non-secret configuration; app.R stays editable.

Databricks additionally needs brickster 0.2.14 or later and jsonlite. No Docker is needed. Its app discovers SQL warehouses after sign-in, with a manual-ID fallback. Listing doesn't run SQL. Clicking Run example query opens the DBI connection and runs SELECT current_user(). Queries can start a stopped warehouse and consume compute credits. Stopping the app doesn't stop or change a shared cloud warehouse.

Databricks Free Edition has no account-console or account-level API access, so it doesn't offer the custom OAuth registration path used here. A full workspace or eligible full-platform trial needs access to that registration. This is distinct from connecting a local R client using a personal token.

See also

oauth_db_demo(), oauth_db_databricks_client(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_databricks_api().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks")
oauth_db_cloud_demo("fabric")
oauth_db_cloud_demo("bigquery", action = "files", path = "my-bigquery-demo")
path <- oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks", action = "files", prompt = FALSE)
file.edit(file.path(path, "app.R"))
oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks", path = path)
} # }
